country.name: Kenya
country.summary: Kenya is the principal maritime gateway for the Northern Corridor, serving Uganda, Rwanda, Burundi, South Sudan and eastern DR Congo through the state-run Port of Mombasa, which handled a record 45.45m tonnes and 2.11m TEU in 2025. All seaports (Mombasa, Lamu, Kisumu, Shimoni) are operated directly by Kenya Ports Authority (KPA); a 30-year PPP concession of Mombasa berths 11-14/CT1 and Lamu berths 1-3 plus its SEZ was relaunched in 2025 after a 2022 DP World-focused process stalled. DP World's current footprint is the Mombasa Port Community System (launched Oct 2025) and the 222-ha DP World-GulfCap Mombasa Industrial Park SEZ (shareholders' agreement Sept 2026). Headline projects include the JICA-financed Dongo Kundu SEZ and free port, Mombasa berths 19B/23/24 (+1.4m TEU), the Naivasha ICD/SEZ transit hub, LAPSSET (Lamu-Isiolo-Moyale/Nadapal) and the restructured A8 Nairobi-Mombasa toll-road widening after the Usahihi expressway PPP was abandoned in 2025.
key_operators: DP World (PCS, Mombasa Industrial Park SEZ)

ports.name: Port of Mombasa (Kilindini Harbour)
ports.operator: Kenya Ports Authority (KPA) – state landlord and terminal operator for all berths, including Container Terminal 1 (CT1) and Container Terminal 2 (CT2)
ports.concession: None in force. A 30-year PPP concession of berths 11-14 and CT1 (with Lamu berths 1-3 and Lamu SEZ) was relaunched in April 2025 (transaction adviser sought March 2025) after a 2022 single-operator process with DP World was suspended in November 2023; Treasury now favours multiple partners.
ports.capacity: 22 berths (conventional and container); two container terminals with combined 2.3m TEU/year; Kipevu Oil Terminal 4 berths/770 m; cruise terminal; bulk grain, soda ash, clinker, coal and titanium facilities
ports.throughput: 45.45m tonnes and 2.11m TEU (2025); transit cargo 15.88m tonnes (2025); 41m tonnes / 2.0m TEU (2024)
ports.projects: Berth 19B (China-financed contract), berths 23 and 24 to add 1.4m TEU and lift container capacity to 3.1m TEU; new terminal operating system (40% complete, early 2026) and gate automation at gates 23/24 (60%); DP World Port Community System live since 27 Oct 2025 (targets 30% faster clearance, c.3,000 users); Dongo Kundu free-port berths (JICA, see zone entry).
ports.notes: DP World is not a terminal operator here; it supplies the PCS (with EMEA Port Logistics) and is developing the adjacent 222-ha Mombasa Industrial Park SEZ with GulfCap Africa. CT2 was financed by Japan (JICA, USD 264m, 2015). Japan and China have objected to a single-operator concession. Cargo dwell time fell from 7.2 days (2012) to 3.3 days (2021) and truck turnaround from 26 h to 15 h (2019-2023) under TMEA-supported programmes.

ports.name: Kipevu Oil Terminal (KOT), Mombasa
ports.operator: Kenya Ports Authority (KPA); pipeline evacuation by Kenya Pipeline Company
ports.capacity: Offshore island terminal with 4 berths, total quay length 770 m; accommodates 3 tankers simultaneously up to 170,000 DWT; handles crude, LPG and refined products (jet fuel, diesel, petrol) via pipelines to storage
ports.opened: n/a (new offshore KOT replaced the original 1963 terminal in the 2020s)
ports.notes: Supplemented by Shimanzi and Mbaraki Wharf oil terminals. Petroleum for Uganda, Rwanda and South Sudan is evacuated by Kenya Pipeline Company to Nairobi, Eldoret and Kisumu, where MV Uhuru I/II lake tankers load for Uganda.

ports.name: Port of Lamu (Manda Bay)
ports.operator: Kenya Ports Authority (KPA); LAPSSET Corridor Development Authority is project owner
ports.concession: None yet. Berths 1-3 and the Lamu SEZ are part of the 30-year PPP concession relaunched in April 2025; the 2022 process had earmarked them for DP World. Government has signalled leasing the port to a private operator to develop the remaining 20 berths.
ports.capacity: 3 operational berths of 400 m each (first phase of 23 planned); draft 17.5 m, natural channel depth 17 m; 500 m turning basin; rated 1.2m TEU/year; can take Post-Panamax/Post-Suezmax vessels above 10,000 TEU
ports.throughput: 799,161 tonnes and 55,687 TEU (2025), up from 74,380 tonnes (2024); 34 vessel calls in H1 2025 vs 20 in all of 2024
ports.projects: Phase 2 liquid-bulk and agri-bulk terminals planned; Lamu-Ijara-Garissa access road (KES 17.9bn, 453 km, started April 2021, delayed) and LAPSSET rail/pipeline still to be built. First-phase cost reported at KES 310bn (LAPSSET programme).
ports.notes: Mainly transshipment (SeaLead, Hapag-Lloyd calls incl. 8,604 TEU Nagoya Express) plus feeder traffic to Mombasa and Dar es Salaam; Ethiopia and South Sudan transit trade not yet material because corridor roads are incomplete. Built by China Communications Construction Co. (2014-2021). Potential DP World target; competitor interest not publicly confirmed.

ports.name: Port of Kisumu (Lake Victoria)
ports.operator: Kenya Ports Authority (KPA); Kenya Railways Corporation operates MV Uhuru I and MV Uhuru II wagon/tanker ferries
ports.capacity: 4 berths, 400 m quay (extension from 262 m to 392 m under way), 4 m draught; linkspan for wagon ferries; oil jetty; target 700,000 tonnes/year
ports.projects: Quay extension, dredging, new passenger terminal, dedicated access road, new mobile crane and forklifts (2025-26); Nakuru-Kisumu metre-gauge line rehabilitated to feed the port.
ports.notes: Main cargo is petroleum exported by MV Uhuru II twice weekly to Port Bell/Jinja (Uganda) and coal/dry cargo from Mwanza (Tanzania). Regional Lake Victoria network also includes MV Mpungu (1,000 t) and Ugandan/Tanzanian tankers. No private concession.

ports.name: Shimoni Fishing Port
ports.operator: Kenya Ports Authority (KPA) with the State Department for Blue Economy
ports.capacity: Up to 24,000 tonnes of fish/year; 75 m x 30 m jetty on 135 m causeway; 4 km deep-water access channel; fish processing plant, cold storage, reefer stations, ice plant, substation
ports.opened: 2025 (fish hatchery opened July 2025; port facilities commissioned in 2025)
ports.notes: Kenya's first purpose-built fishing port, part of the Blue Economy programme; near the Lunga Lunga/Horohoro border with Tanzania.

ports.name: Nairobi Inland Container Depot (ICD Embakasi)
ports.operator: Kenya Ports Authority (KPA); rail haulage by Kenya Railways (SGR and metre gauge)
ports.capacity: Over 450,000 TEU/year on 43.5 ha; container yard, 4 warehouses, 3 sheds
ports.notes: Primary dry port for Nairobi imports moved by SGR 'railtainer' service from Mombasa; policy since 2026 is to route long-haul transit cargo (Uganda, Rwanda, DRC, South Sudan) via Naivasha ICD instead.

ports.name: Naivasha Inland Container Depot (Mai Mahiu/Suswa)
ports.operator: Kenya Railways Corporation (owner) with Kenya Ports Authority and KRA operations
ports.capacity: 3,588 ground slots (KPA); KRC states 45,000 m2 yard, 2m tonnes/year and capacity expanded from 180,000 to 450,000 TEU/year; Star reported 4,000 TEU handling capacity at 19% occupancy (Feb 2026)
ports.opened: 2019 (SGR Phase 2A terminus); fully operationalised as transit hub February 2026
ports.projects: Designated in Feb 2026 as the priority depot for transit cargo to Uganda, Rwanda, DRC and South Sudan; plots in adjoining Naivasha SEZ allocated to Uganda, Rwanda, Burundi, DRC and South Sudan (10 acres) for national dry-port facilities.
ports.notes: SGR ends at Suswa/Naivasha; onward movement to Malaba is by road or the rehabilitated Longonot-Malaba metre-gauge link. Africa Global Logistics (AGL) is a licensed Naivasha SEZ tenant – competitor presence.

zones.name: DP World – GulfCap Africa Mombasa Industrial Park SEZ
zones.authority: Joint venture of DP World and GulfCap Africa (Suleiman Shahbal); licensed under Kenya's SEZ framework
zones.incentives: Kenya SEZ regime (reduced corporate tax, VAT zero-rating, duty exemptions)
zones.tenants: 60+ local and international companies expressed interest (Sept 2026); 20,000+ direct/indirect jobs targeted
zones.projects: Partnership announced early August 2026 (reported KES 12bn); shareholders' agreement signed in Nairobi Sept 2026 with President Ruto pledging supporting infrastructure. Investment value and construction timeline not disclosed.
zones.notes: DP World asset. Extends DP World's Kenya presence beyond the Mombasa Port Community System into port-linked industrial real estate; exact site within Mombasa County not disclosed in sources.

zones.name: Dongo Kundu Special Economic Zone (Mombasa SEZ) and Free Port
zones.authority: Kenya Ports Authority (transferred from Special Economic Zones Authority, Aug 2024); master plan by JICA
zones.area: c. 3,000 acres (1,214 ha); land applications for nearly 7,000 acres received
zones.incentives: SEZ tax incentives and customs exemptions
zones.tenants: Taifa Gas LPG terminal and Ruike Energy oil refinery in progress; Afreximbank leased 500 acres (Feb 2025)
zones.projects: JICA grant KES 6bn plus KES 50bn concessional loan (30-yr, 12-yr grace); contractor Toa Corporation; package 1 berth/yards/channel KES 42bn, package 2 equipment KES 3.4bn, access roads KES 7.5bn, power KES 7bn; completion targeted 2026; 18 km Dongo Kundu bypass (KES 45bn, 98% complete Dec 2025) links Miritini to Ng'ombeni. Gazetted as SEZ July 2019.
zones.notes: Adjacent to Mombasa port, SGR and Moi International Airport. Japan's involvement is one reason Tokyo opposes a single-operator port concession.

zones.name: Naivasha Special Economic Zone
zones.authority: Special Economic Zones Authority (SEZA); Kenya Railways/KPA for the ICD; gazetted 26 July 2019
zones.area: Expanded from 1,000 to c. 6,000 acres; 5,000-acre Phase II planned
zones.incentives: SEZ tax regime; geothermal power at c. KES 5/kWh via dedicated 90 MVA substation; SGR access to Mombasa
zones.tenants: 14-19 licensees by mid-2024 plus 6 in 2025 (TAD Motors, Crystal Frozen Foods, Horizon SEZ, Africa Global Logistics); 20 investors incl. Uganda, Rwanda, Burundi, DRC and South Sudan national dry-port plots; commitments >KES 50bn
zones.projects: Phase II 5,000 acres; South Sudan 10-acre dry port; transit-cargo hub role from Feb 2026
zones.notes: Competitor AGL (Africa Global Logistics) is a licensed tenant.

zones.name: Tatu City SEZ
zones.incentives: Reduced corporate tax, zero-rated VAT, import duty exemptions under SEZ Act
zones.tenants: 110+ businesses (developer); c. 88 companies operational/under development, c. 40 SEZ licensees, 25,000+ jobs; investment >KES 400bn (2025)
zones.projects: FullCare Medical USD 100m facility; Hewa Tele USD 20m medical gases plant
zones.notes: Most mature private SEZ in Kenya; c. 70% Kenyan-owned manufacturers.

zones.name: Konza Technopolis SEZ
zones.incentives: 10-year corporate tax exemption, VAT relief, duty-free imports (SEZ)
zones.opened: n/a (Phase 1 infrastructure complete: c. 400 acres, 40 km smart roads)
zones.projects: Phase 1 horizontal infrastructure complete; further phases planned. Gazetted as SEZ July 2019.
zones.notes: 65 km southeast of Nairobi on the A109 Mombasa highway with Konza SGR station.

zones.name: Athi River Export Processing Zone
zones.authority: Export Processing Zones Authority (EPZA), established 1990 under EPZ Act CAP 517; zone operator Athi River EPZ Ltd
zones.incentives: 10-year corporate and withholding tax holidays, perpetual VAT and import-duty exemption on inputs, 100% investment deduction, stamp duty exemption
zones.tenants: n/a (EPZA lists 63 gazetted EPZs nationally; Athi River is the flagship public zone and EPZA HQ)
zones.notes: On the A104 Nairobi-Namanga highway; EPZ regime is distinct from SEZ regime.

zones.name: Lamu Special Economic Zone / Port City
zones.authority: LAPSSET Corridor Development Authority; earmarked for the PPP concession with Lamu berths 1-3
zones.area: c. 500 ha proposed under the 2022 DP World proposal
zones.projects: Included in the 30-year PPP package relaunched April 2025; Phase 2 of Lamu port foresees liquid-bulk and agri-bulk terminals.
zones.notes: Previously proposed for DP World (2022 concession letter); status of DP World interest unconfirmed as of 2025.

corridors.name: Northern Corridor (Mombasa – Nairobi – Malaba/Busia – Kampala – Kigali/Bujumbura – Goma/Juba)
corridors.route: Mombasa → Nairobi → Nakuru → Eldoret → Malaba/Busia → Kampala → Kigali/Bujumbura/Goma; branch Eldoret → Nadapal → Juba
corridors.operator: Northern Corridor Transit and Transport Coordination Authority (NCTTCA); roads by KeNHA; rail by KRC
corridors.capacity_or_traffic: Mombasa transit cargo 15.88m tonnes (2025, +19.5%); total corridor throughput at Mombasa 45.45m tonnes / 2.11m TEU (2025); South Sudan 12.7% of transit cargo (2025)
corridors.projects: Naivasha ICD transit hub (2026); Mombasa West urban roads (TMEA, truck turnaround -43% 2019-23); A8 Nairobi-Mombasa four-lane toll widening (transaction adviser being procured 2025-26).
corridors.notes: Kenya's core trade artery and DP World's main hinterland exposure via the Mombasa PCS; competes with Tanzania's Central Corridor (Dar es Salaam, where DP World holds the 2023 concession).

corridors.name: Standard Gauge Railway Mombasa – Nairobi – Naivasha (Suswa)
corridors.route: Mombasa port → Nairobi ICD (Embakasi) → Naivasha ICD/Suswa
corridors.operator: Kenya Railways Corporation (took over from CRBC subsidiary Afristar in 2022)
corridors.capacity_or_traffic: c. 5m tonnes freight (2018); 'railtainer' container service to Nairobi and Naivasha ICDs; latest tonnage n/a
corridors.projects: Phase 2B/2C Naivasha-Kisumu-Malaba not financed; interim link via rehabilitated Longonot-Malaba metre gauge. Naivasha ICD transit role expanded Feb 2026.
corridors.notes: Cost USD 3.6bn for Phase 1, 90% China Exim Bank; opened 31 May 2017 (Mombasa-Nairobi) and Oct 2019 (Nairobi-Naivasha).

corridors.name: Metre-gauge railway Nairobi/Longonot – Nakuru – Malaba and Nakuru – Kisumu
corridors.route: Naivasha/Longonot → Nakuru → Eldoret → Malaba (Uganda); Nakuru → Kisumu port (Lake Victoria wagon ferries to Port Bell/Jinja)
corridors.operator: Kenya Railways Corporation (formerly Rift Valley Railways concession)
corridors.projects: Nakuru-Kisumu line rehabilitated to reconnect Kisumu port; Longonot-Malaba link bridges SGR gap to Uganda.
corridors.notes: Interchange between SGR and metre gauge at Naivasha; Malaba is the rail border with Uganda.

corridors.name: LAPSSET Corridor (Lamu – Isiolo – Moyale/Nadapal – Juba/Addis Ababa)
corridors.route: Lamu port → Garissa/Ijara → Isiolo → Moyale (Ethiopia) and Isiolo → Lokichar → Nadapal (South Sudan)
corridors.capacity_or_traffic: Lamu port 799,161 t / 55,687 TEU (2025); corridor road traffic n/a
corridors.projects: Lamu port berths 1-3 complete (2021); Lamu-Ijara-Garissa road (KES 17.9bn, started 2021, delayed by insecurity/floods); SGR, crude pipeline, Isiolo airport and resort cities at planning stage; programme listed in PIDA PAP 2 (2021-2030).
corridors.notes: Northern rival gateway to Mombasa for Ethiopia/South Sudan; commercial viability hinges on road completion and a private port operator.

corridors.name: A8 Nairobi – Mombasa highway (former Usahihi expressway PPP)
corridors.route: Mombasa (Bonje) → Voi → Mtito Andei → Machakos (Mlolongo) → Nairobi
corridors.projects: Bechtel selected 2017 (USD 3bn+ EPC, dropped over financing); KIND (Korea) 2022; Everstrong Capital USD 3.6bn Usahihi PPP (PDA May 2024) rejected by PPP Committee 2 July 2025 and appeal declined April 2026. KeNHA now procuring a transaction adviser for a brownfield four-lane access-controlled toll widening of the existing A8.
corridors.notes: Existing two-lane highway carries most Northern Corridor road freight; congestion and accident risk remain the key logistics constraint.

corridors.name: A2 Great North Road Nairobi – Isiolo – Moyale (Mombasa–Nairobi–Addis Ababa corridor)
corridors.route: Nairobi → Thika → Nanyuki → Isiolo → Marsabit → Moyale → Addis Ababa
corridors.projects: Listed by KeNHA as a planned upgrade programme (Thika-Kenol-Sagana-Nanyuki-Isiolo-Moyale); Moyale OSBP opened June 2021.
corridors.notes: Only paved link to Ethiopia; underpins Ethiopia's use of Mombasa/Lamu as alternative to Djibouti.

border_crossings.name: Malaba
border_crossings.traffic: Busiest Northern Corridor road and rail crossing; thousands of trucks weekly; main gateway for Uganda, Rwanda, eastern DRC and South Sudan transit
border_crossings.projects: OSBP completed 2016; TMEA reports crossing times reduced by more than half; SGR extension to Malaba unfinanced
border_crossings.notes: Metre-gauge rail crossing; recurrent truck queues of several km during peak periods.

border_crossings.name: Busia
border_crossings.traffic: Second Uganda gateway; heavy small-scale cross-border trade
border_crossings.projects: OSBP commissioned February 2018 by Presidents Kenyatta and Museveni (TMEA-supported)

border_crossings.name: Namanga
border_crossings.traffic: Main Nairobi–Arusha road link (183 km from Nairobi, 110 km from Arusha)
border_crossings.notes: OSBP status widely reported under the EAC programme but not verified in fetched sources.

border_crossings.name: Taveta / Holili
border_crossings.traffic: Voi–Taveta–Holili–Arusha road; significant informal cross-border market trade
border_crossings.projects: OSBP launched by EAC February 2016; TMEA reports halved crossing times
border_crossings.notes: Post is c. 5 km west of Taveta town, 111 km from Voi on the A23.

border_crossings.name: Isebania / Sirari
border_crossings.traffic: Kisumu–Musoma–Mwanza road route; regional food and fuel trade
border_crossings.notes: Reported as an EAC OSBP but not verified in fetched sources.

border_crossings.name: Moyale
border_crossings.traffic: Only major Kenya–Ethiopia road gateway on the A2 / Mombasa–Nairobi–Addis corridor
border_crossings.projects: OSBP began commercial operations June 2021 (Ethiopia's first OSBP); TMEA reports crossing times cut by more than half
border_crossings.notes: Ethiopia has long mooted extending rail to Moyale to connect with LAPSSET.

border_crossings.name: Lunga Lunga / Horohoro
border_crossings.traffic: Coastal Mombasa–Tanga–Dar es Salaam road; 102 km south of Mombasa
border_crossings.projects: Converted to one-stop border crossing under EAC standards

border_crossings.name: Nadapal
border_crossings.traffic: Lokichogio–Nadapal–Kapoeta–Juba route; secondary to Malaba/Nimule for Juba-bound cargo
border_crossings.projects: South Sudan immigration post and housing opened July 2011; Nadapal–Juba 375 km road upgrade contracted 2008 but delayed; LAPSSET branch planned
border_crossings.notes: Security escorts historically required; gravel road on Kenyan side to Lokichogio.

border_crossings.name: Liboi
border_crossings.notes: Official Kenya–Somalia crossings have been largely closed since 2011 for security reasons; phased reopening has been announced but not verified in fetched sources. 180 km from Garissa, 17 km from Dhobley.

border_crossings.name: Mandera (Bula Hawa / Suftu)
border_crossings.traffic: Livestock and informal trade in the Mandera triangle
border_crossings.notes: Tri-border area with recurring security incidents; formal crossing status not verified in fetched sources.
